source_limits: De Sterck–Ullrich Theorem 3.1 omits the compactness/uniform-integrability hypotheses and gives no proof; it is not used as proof evidence for the local theorem.
MIT Lecture 19 is a six-page scheme note; it does not prove the conditional weak-limit theorem.
The weak-limit theorem assumes strong local L1 convergence and local uniform state bounds; it proves neither compactness nor entropy admissibility.
The CFL-violating Godunov trajectory is a counterexample to entropy selection from the weak theorem hypotheses alone, not to CFL-restricted monotone-scheme convergence.
The published Burgers expansion-shock example is B-page material and is not used as a dependency; this batch proves its entropy defect directly from the A-page Kruzhkov definition.

alternatives.argument: This is a definition, not an imported theorem. For a test function compactly supported in R×(-∞,T), choose a bounded spatial interval containing its spatial support and T'<T containing its nonnegative-time support. The assumed local essential bound makes u bounded on the test support; continuity of f makes f(u) bounded on the bounded range of u, so both space-time pairings are absolutely integrable. The initial term is integrable because u0 is locally integrable and the spatial trace of the test is compactly supported. The item explicitly defines the weak identity with that initial boundary term. Its local formulation is the published bounded weak formulation with global L∞ replaced by the explicitly stated local boundedness condition; no result from the inaccessible article is required. The Chechkin–Goritsky notes support the interior integral-identity convention, while the current published supplier provides the exact initial-boundary-term formulation.
